SaaS Sellability Master Checklist
Five stages, five columns. Find the column for your ARR, tick what is true today, and add your points at the bottom.
Every column stands on its own. Each row is one thing buyers test at that size, with the benchmark they expect. Items worth 2 points carry an amber tag; they move the multiple most. The detailed edition for your stage explains why buyers care about each item and what to strengthen.

Deal Risk At This Stage

GRR. If your annual GRR is under 70%, the business will struggle to sell. Most buyers at this stage pass before they look at anything else.

ARR CAGR. If your 2 to 3 year ARR CAGR is under 20%, or any year in that period was flat or down, buyers read it as a product-market fit problem. The business will be difficult to sell at this stage.

If You Want To Sell At This Stage

At this size buyers pay a multiple of SDE and most deals close on marketplaces. A $300K ARR product with 30% SDE margin sells for 2x to 4x SDE, or $180K to $360K. The checklist items that move the price most are clean books, documented churn, and a product that runs without you.

If You Want To Sell At This Stage

This is the first stage where PE and strategics compete for the deal. The median revenue multiple is 3.3x; top-quartile deals reach 7x. A $3.5M ARR company with 25% growth, 90% GRR and a GM in place can expect $10M to $15M. Without the GM, buyers add an earn-out.

Buyers run a full process with QoE and legal diligence. The median EBITDA multiple is 16.9x; revenue multiples run 2.9x at the median and above 9x for top-quartile growth and retention. An $8M ARR company that meets the Rule of 40 with 95% GRR can expect $25M to $50M.
